notes:
Account snapshot: global quant hedge fund building a unified investigation + research search layer. Heavy regulatory constraints; prefer private/VPC or on-prem for sensitive indices. Currently running a Pinecone POC for embeddings + ANN; unhappy with rerank latency and cold-start costs. Key quote from CTO: "Latency is everything — we need p95 under 200ms for rerank flows or the desk won't adopt it."

Recent interactions: quick discovery (2025-11-05), architecture deep-dive (2025-12-10), security questionnaire submitted (2026-01-14), demo (2026-02-03). SE Miguel ran a mini PoC for 5M chunks (embedding upserts + hybrid search) and saw 20-30% cost delta vs expectations. They care about predictable unit economics more than raw throughput — willing to pay for reserved throughput if latency SLOs guaranteed.

Technical notes (shorthand):
- Indexing scale target: ~200M docs / ~50M chunks year 1; growth 2x Y1->Y2.
- Latency targets: p95 rerank < 200ms, p99 < 500ms.
- Throughput targets: 800 qps sustained, spikes to 2000 qps for alerting queries.
- Cost target: $0.0008-$0.002 per query (including embedding + ANN + rerank).
- Current stack: embeddings produced in-house (512-d dense), Pinecone for ANN, FastAPI microservices for rerank, internal vector cache.

They asked for: connector that supports fast batch upserts, incremental sync from S3, per-tenant namespace isolation, on-prem deployment topology docs, and direct KMS integration. Also want built-in rerank path that can execute dense ANN fetch + lightweight re-ranker on same host to avoid network hop penalty.

Sales/contract hints: procurement timeline tied to Q2 budget cycle. Will evaluate Dedicated reserved nodes vs Private deployment. Budget estimate TBD; if Redwood can demonstrate 30% cost improvement vs current Pinecone baseline and commit to latency SLOs, procurement moves faster.

Open action items: schedule pgvector connectivity demo, produce architecture diagram for hybrid (bm25 + ANN) fallback, answer data residency attestation (legal), share benchmark runbook and sample metrics for 50M/200M index sizes.
